content.text: In Spring REST, the request body refers to the data sent by the client to the server in an HTTP request. It is typically used in POST, PUT, or PATCH requests where data (usually in JSON or XML format) is submitted to the server.

items: Send Data: To transmit client data (like form data, JSON, XML) to the server.
Entity Transmission: Used to send complex objects/entities.

subsections.heading: How is the Request Body Handled?

content.text: Spring uses @RequestBody annotation to bind the request body to a method parameter:

items: Spring automatically deserializes the incoming JSON/XML into Java objects using HttpMessageConverters.
Form URL Encoded (less common in REST APIs):

content.text: Content negotiation is the process where the client and server decide the format of the data to exchange (e.g., JSON, XML, plain text).

items: To support multiple response formats for different clients.
Flexibility in REST APIs to serve browsers (HTML) or other systems (JSON/XML).
Flexibility to serve multiple client types.
Decouples data format from business logic.

sections.heading: Handling File Uploads in Spring REST

content.text: Sending binary or textual files (like PDFs, images) from client to server via REST endpoints.

items: Save files directly to disk instead of memory.

content.text: Data sent in the body of HTTP requests (JSON, XML, files). Large payloads are usually big JSON/XML datasets or files.
